non_blocking_risks: Evidence is entirely self-reported: as a no-tools judge I cannot recompute the declared SHA-256 bindings (implementation, plan, correction-layer, contract, incident-set, test) or re-run the 15/15 and 116/116 suites; the verdict rests on the harness's internal consistency rather than independent recomputation.

Atomicity/isolation is shown by one injected one-byte receipt corruption plus two sequential fresh-root trials; no concurrent/racing promotion is exercised, so SERIALIZABLE contention behavior is asserted via the isolation level rather than demonstrated under true contention.

Duplicate-rollback protection relies on a database primary-key conflict (error path) while duplicate-promotion is idempotent (no-op path); the asymmetry is acceptable but leaves rollback re-entry guarded at the storage layer rather than the application layer.
Scope is explicitly local/synthetic; P9 live AWS/CockroachDB integration and production behavior are out of scope and unproven (honestly disclosed as a limitation).
evidence_gaps: Per-trial state shows policy-p8-v1 golden after rollback but does not explicitly display the promoted candidate transitioning to SUPERSEDED, so the 'exactly one golden' invariant post-rollback is inferred from counts rather than shown.

No single-active-golden constraint is quoted from migration 001 (only the GOLDEN|SUPERSEDED domain, unique identities, and 32-byte hash constraints); the single-golden property is enforced by application/harness logic that is asserted but not displayed.

The eight persisted proposals versus the additional malformed/unsupported-schema inputs (which also receive rejection receipts) are not reconciled into one explicit total, leaving the full input population slightly ambiguous.

Receipt-hash correctness for the eight outcomes is asserted as tested (one 64-char hash, exact proposal hash, exact incident-set hash each), but the actual bound hash values are not enumerated in the packet.
